newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - January 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - January 3.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Friday's edition of Daily Variety:
HOLLYWOOD - Of the official domestic B.O. total of $5.76 billion for the year, mainstream releases accounted for a sliver more than 96 percent of the grosses, up slightly from a year ago.

HOLLYWOOD - A battle is brewing between ABC Entertainment and ABC News, as the former wants to schedule David Kelley's midseason drama The Practice in the Wednesday 10 p.m. slot currently held by the ABC News magazine PrimeTime Live. ABC is a unit of Walt Disney Co.
NEW YORK - After months of speculation, Viacom Inc has begun efforts to sell its radio station group, holding talks with a range of radio operators.

HOLLYWOOD - Eerie, Indiana -- the short-lived NBC supernatural series that last aired in 1992 -- has come back to life on the Fox Kids Network. The Fox network is owned by News Corp Ltd. NBC is a subsidiary of General Electric Co.

HOLLYWOOD - Eyemark Entertainment has sold its new weekly action hour Pensacola: Wings of Gold to the CBS Television Stations and the Partner Stations Network for fall. CBS Inc is a unit of Westinghouse Electric Co.
